title: Home Alone
logline: A boy is accidentally left at home when his family flies to Paris for Christmas, and two burglars pick the wrong house.
why: The plot is carried by places and objects, so a missed line never means a lost scene. Family vocabulary, daily routines and short, concrete dialogue repeat often enough to stick.
language: American English, mostly simple sentences; the burglars talk fast in a few scenes, and Kevin's older brother mumbles on purpose.
content: Slapstick violence and cartoon traps; nobody is seriously hurt. Suitable for all ages.

scenes.title: The head count
scenes.task: Count the family members who run through the airport. Who is missing, and who finally notices?

scenes.title: Dinner for one
scenes.task: Pause on Kevin's plate. Name everything he eats, then compare it with your own ideal dinner.

scenes.title: The burglars' plan
scenes.task: The burglars name the houses they will rob and when. Predict: what will Kevin do about it?

scenes.title: Welcome to the traps
scenes.task: List three traps in the order they happen. Which one made the room laugh loudest?

words.def: a person who breaks into a house to steal
words.ex: The burglars watch the house from a van.

words.def: the room under the roof of a house
words.ex: Kevin hides in the attic when he is scared.

words.def: a person who lives next to you
words.ex: The old neighbour is not as scary as he looks.

words.def: a thing that catches or hurts someone
words.ex: The stairs become a trap.

words.def: to make a loud, high sound when afraid
words.ex: Marv screams when the spider lands on him.

words.def: with no other people there
words.ex: At first, Kevin loves being alone.

questions: Why does Kevin's family fly to Paris without him? Whose fault is it, really?
What is the first thing Kevin does when he understands that he is alone? What would you do?
Kevin says he wants his family to disappear — and then they do. Is the film a wish come true or a lesson?
Which trap is the cleverest, and which one is just cruel?
Why is Kevin afraid of the old man next door, and what changes his mind?
In your country, at what age can a child stay home alone? Is Kevin old enough?
Is Kevin a good boy or a difficult boy? Give two examples from the film.
Which line from the film would you repeat to a friend as a joke? Try to say it the same way.

gaps.line: When I grow up and get married, I'm living ___!
This is my house. I have to ___ it.

quotes.quote: Kevin! What did you do to my room?
quotes.note: Buzz is the older brother — and the reason Kevin gets sent to the attic.

quotes.quote: Keep the change, you filthy animal.
quotes.note: Kevin learns it from a black-and-white gangster film and uses it as his own line.
He says it as a joke — and then starts to believe it.

quiz.q: Where does the family fly for Christmas?
quiz.why: They fly to Paris and leave Kevin behind in Chicago.

quiz.q: Who does Kevin meet in the church?
quiz.why: The old man whose son he is afraid of — the meeting changes how Kevin sees him.

quiz.q: What time do the burglars plan to enter the house?
quiz.why: They say they will come at nine, so Kevin prepares the house before that.

quiz.q: How does Kevin finally get help?
quiz.why: The old neighbour arrives with a snow shovel — and the burglars run into the police.

quiz.q: Why is Kevin sad at the end?
options: He understands that being alone is not fun
He must go back to school
quiz.why: He wanted his family gone, then discovered that he wanted them back.

roleplay.title: The head count
roleplay.setting: Airport check-in at 7 a.m. The family is late, the queue is long, and nobody is counting children.

roles.brief: You are the mother. You are stressed, you have five children, a passport for each one and no time for jokes. Keep asking the clerk to hurry.
You work for the airline. You have heard every excuse. You are polite but very slow, and you keep finding problems with the documents.
You are eight. You are in the middle of this chaos. You are asked nothing and say almost nothing — until the one moment it matters.

roleplay.challenge: Play the scene twice: once as a comedy, once as a disaster film. Then swap roles and see who notices the missing child.

quest.title: Station 1 · The missing passenger
quest.task: At the airport the family counts heads. How many people are travelling, and how many do they count? Find the moment and write both numbers.

quest.title: Station 2 · Word hunt
quest.task: Find in the film: a word for the room under the roof, a word for a person who steals from houses, and a word for a person living next door.

quest.title: Station 3 · Trap designers
quest.task: Invent one new trap for the burglars using only things you can see in a classroom. Describe it in three sentences, then act it out in slow motion.
quest.answer: Any plausible three-sentence design, acted out

quest.title: Station 4 · The order of things
quest.task: Put these four events in order: the pizza delivery, the fake party, the tarantula on Marv's face, the old neighbour's snow shovel.
quest.answer: pizza, fake party, tarantula, snow shovel

title: Toy Story
logline: A cowboy doll is the favourite toy in Andy's room, until a new space toy arrives and takes his place.
why: The story stays inside one boy's bedroom and one street, so the pictures explain almost everything. The lines are short and funny, and the words for toys, friends and feeling left out come back again and again.
language: American English with quick comic voices: Woody talks like a cowboy, Buzz talks like a television hero, and the other toys shout over each other.
content: Cartoon danger and a mean boy next door who breaks toys; a dog chases Woody and Buzz. Nobody is badly hurt, and the ending is happy.

scenes.title: When Andy leaves
scenes.task: List three toys you can see in Andy's room. What do they do the moment the door closes?

scenes.title: A new space toy
scenes.task: Listen to the new toy's name and his famous line. Say both back to your partner.

scenes.title: A toy, not a ranger
scenes.task: Buzz sees a television advert full of Buzz toys. What does he suddenly understand, and what does he do next?

scenes.title: The rocket
scenes.task: Woody lights the rocket in Sid's garden. Predict: where will the two toys land, and will they catch the van?

words.def: a thing that children play with
words.ex: Andy has many toys in his room.

words.def: unhappy because someone has what you want
words.ex: Woody is jealous of the new space toy.

words.def: the place beyond the sky
words.ex: Buzz says he comes from space.

words.def: a small thing that gives power
words.ex: Buzz runs on batteries, not rocket fuel.

words.def: not afraid of danger
words.ex: Buzz is brave, even when he is lost.

words.def: a person you like and play with
words.ex: In the end, Woody and Buzz are friends.

questions: Why is Woody jealous of Buzz? Do you think that is fair?
Which toy in Andy's room would you like to have? Why that one?
In your country, does a child take one special toy everywhere? What was yours?
Buzz thinks he is a real space ranger. Why is that funny — and a little sad?
What would you say to Woody after he knocks Buzz out of the window?
Sid breaks toys for fun. Is he a bad boy or just a bored boy?
Which moment made you laugh most? Show it to the class, slowly.
If your family moved house tomorrow, which three things would you take?

gaps.hint: a thing a child plays with
things you wear on your feet

gaps.line: I am Buzz Lightyear. I come in ___.

quotes.note: Buzz says it before every jump, and it becomes the film's most famous line.
Woody shouts it at the gas station, when he is losing his place as Andy's favourite.

quotes.quote: There's a snake in my boots!
quotes.note: Woody's pull string says it. He cannot choose his own lines.

quiz.q: What does Andy get for his birthday that changes everything?
quiz.why: Buzz Lightyear arrives, and Andy loves him at once.

quiz.q: Where do Woody and Buzz get left behind?
quiz.why: The family drives away from the gas station without them.

quiz.q: Who takes Buzz home from the pizza restaurant?
quiz.why: Sid finds Buzz and takes him to his house.

quiz.q: What does Buzz see on television?
quiz.why: The advert shows a shop full of Buzz toys, and Buzz finally understands that he is a toy.

quiz.q: How do the two toys catch the moving van?
options: They fly out of Sid's garden on a rocket
quiz.why: Woody lights the rocket and it carries them into the air, just as the family drives away.

roleplay.title: The new toy
roleplay.setting: Andy's bedroom, the night Buzz arrives. Woody has been the favourite for years, and every toy is watching.

roles.brief: You are the old favourite. You are polite and funny, but you want your place back and you do not like this stranger.
You are a space ranger. You do not understand that you are a toy. You answer every question with a report from your mission.
You are eight. You just want to play with both toys, and you do not see that one of them is upset.

roleplay.challenge: Play it twice: once with Woody as the good guy, once with Buzz as the good guy. Which version is funnier?

quest.title: Station 1 · The owner
quest.task: Find the name of the boy who owns the toys. Then find what he writes on Buzz's boot.
quest.answer: Andy; he writes his own name

quest.title: Station 2 · Word hunt
quest.task: Find three words in the film for: a child's plaything, a bad feeling about a rival, and the power source inside a toy.

quest.title: Station 3 · Design a toy
quest.task: Invent a new toy for Andy. Give it a name, one special power and one weakness. Describe it in three sentences.
quest.answer: Any named toy with a power and a weakness

quest.title: Station 4 · The order
quest.task: Put these in order: the birthday party, the gas station, the pizza restaurant, Sid's rocket.
quest.answer: birthday party, gas station, pizza restaurant, rocket

title: Finding Nemo
logline: A small fish with one weak fin is taken from the sea, and his worried father swims across the ocean to bring him home.
why: The story is a simple journey with one clear goal, and every new place brings a new, funny character. The sea is full of colour and movement, so the pictures carry the meaning when a line goes past too fast.
language: American English, fast and playful: Dory talks very quickly, the sharks speak slowly and seriously, and the turtles use surfer slang.
content: The opening has a barracuda attack that leaves Nemo without his mother, and a shark shows its teeth. Sad and a little frightening for small children, but the rest is cartoon adventure.

scenes.title: The first day of school
scenes.task: Watch Marlin and Nemo at the edge of the reef. How many times does Marlin say 'no'?

scenes.title: Fish are friends
scenes.task: Listen to the sharks' meeting. Write down the words they promise to say.

scenes.title: Riding the current
scenes.task: The turtles call Marlin 'dude'. What does his face tell you about his feelings?

scenes.title: Nemo plays dead
scenes.task: The fish in the tank have a plan. Predict: will it work, and what could go wrong?

words.def: the part a fish swims with

words.def: a glass home for pet fish

words.def: to not remember something

words.def: not afraid of danger

Which line made you laugh? Say it the way the character says it.

Bruce says it at his shark support group.
The seagulls say it when they see something to eat.

quiz.q: Why does Nemo swim out to the boat?
options: He wants to meet the diver
quiz.why: His classmates dare him to touch the boat, and a diver takes him away.

quiz.q: Who helps Marlin on his journey?
quiz.why: Dory is a blue fish with a very short memory.

quiz.q: Where does Nemo end up?

quiz.q: Who is Darla?

roleplay.title: The first day of school
roleplay.setting: The coral reef, early morning. It is Nemo's first day, and Mr. Ray is waiting with the class.

roles.brief: You are worried. Before you say hello, you ask three questions about safety, and you answer every question with a warning.
You are excited. You want to swim with the other children and you do not want your father to come with you.
You are the teacher. You are patient and cheerful, and you sing the names of the fish in your class.

quest.title: Station 1 · The address
quest.task: A diver's mask falls into the sea. Write the address on it.

quest.title: Station 2 · Word hunt
quest.task: Find three words from the film for: the part a fish swims with, a glass home for fish, and the big water.

quest.title: Station 3 · New sea creature
quest.task: Invent a sea animal for this film. Draw it, give it a name and say what it can do.

quest.title: Station 4 · The journey
quest.task: Put these four places in the order Marlin reaches them: the shark meeting, the jellyfish, the turtles, Sydney.

title: Charlie and the Chocolate Factory
logline: Five children win a golden ticket to visit the strangest chocolate factory in the world, and one of them is very poor.
why: Every scene repeats the same pattern: a new room, a rule, and a child who breaks it. That makes the story easy to predict and the language easy to follow, and the factory gives you colours, machines and songs to talk about.
language: British and American English mixed; Willy Wonka speaks quickly in short, strange sentences, and the four other children are loud and rude.
content: Children are greedy and rude, and some are in real danger in the factory: one is pulled into a pipe and one is carried away by squirrels. Nothing is bloody, but the humour is dark and strange.

scenes.title: Five winners
scenes.task: Watch the television news. Write the name and the country of each winner.

scenes.title: The last ticket
scenes.task: Charlie holds the last chocolate bar. Pause before he opens it. Predict: ticket or no ticket?

scenes.title: The nut room
scenes.task: The squirrels decide who is a 'bad nut'. Why does Veruca go down the chute, and not her father?

scenes.title: Wonka's father
scenes.task: Willy Wonka remembers his father, the dentist. What did his father want for him, and what did Willy want?

words.def: a small paper that lets you enter

words.def: wanting too much of everything
words.ex: Augustus is greedy and eats too much.

words.def: to make something new
words.ex: Wonka invents amazing sweets.

a funny sound, not a word

You are rich, bored and very rude. Nothing is good enough for you, and you want everything now.
You are shy and kind. You have never been on television, and you keep looking at your grandfather.

quest.title: Station 2 · Word hunt

quest.answer: Any named sweet with a taste and an effect

quest.title: Station 4 · The accidents
quest.task: Put the four accidents in order: Violet, Augustus, Mike, Veruca.

title: Matilda
logline: A clever girl is ignored by her family and sent to a school with a terrible headmistress, and then she discovers her own power.
why: The film is built from small, everyday places: a house, a school, a library, a playground. The goodies and the baddies are drawn in loud colours and loud voices, so a beginner can always hear who is speaking and how they feel.
language: Mostly American English; Miss Trunchbull shouts in a strong British accent, and Matilda speaks slowly and clearly.
content: A frightening headmistress shouts at children, swings a girl by her pigtails and locks children in a small cupboard full of nails. It is played for comedy, but the threat feels real.

scenes.title: A girl who reads
scenes.task: Look at Matilda in the library. What is she doing, and how is she different from other children of her age?

scenes.title: Meet the Trunchbull
scenes.task: Watch the headmistress walk down the steps. Write three rules she gives the children.

scenes.title: Miss Honey's house
scenes.task: Look at Miss Honey's little house. Why is it so small and empty? What does that tell you about her?

scenes.title: The chalk writes

words.def: a person who is unkind to others

title: Paddington
logline: A young bear from Peru arrives in London with a suitcase, a label and a love of marmalade, and one family takes him home.
why: The film explains itself with objects: a label, a suitcase, a bathroom, a sandwich under a hat. The family is ordinary and the bear is not, so the everyday language of homes, trains and food comes back in a funny situation.
language: British English, polite and quick; Paddington speaks slowly and formally, while the Londoners use more slang and short forms.
content: A woman with a dark workshop wants to put Paddington in a museum, and those scenes are creepy. Otherwise it is gentle comedy, with a few jokes about accidents in the house.

scenes.title: A bear at the station
scenes.task: Look at the label round Paddington's neck. What does it say, and who wrote it?

scenes.title: The bathroom
scenes.task: Paddington tries to wash. List three things that go wrong in the bathroom.

scenes.title: One night or more
scenes.task: Listen to Mr. and Mrs. Brown. How long does each one want the bear to stay?

scenes.title: The workshop
scenes.task: Pause when Millicent opens the door. What can you see in the room, and how does it make you feel?

words.def: a place where trains stop

words.def: a person you do not know

quiz.q: What is Paddington's favourite food?

quest.task: Find three words from the film for: a sweet orange food, a bag for clothes, and a person you do not know.

quest.title: Station 3 · A new home

title: The Wizard of Oz
logline: A girl and her dog are carried by a tornado to a strange land, where she must find the Wizard of Oz to get home.
why: The film says everything twice: once in dialogue and once in colour, song or costume. The story is a straight road with three friends, so a beginner always knows where the characters are and what they want.
language: 1930s American English, slow and very clear, with songs that repeat the same lines many times; a few old farm words may be new.
content: The Wicked Witch and her flying monkeys are frightening for small children, and there is a scene with fire. Nothing is bloody; the witch melts at the end.

scenes.title: Over the rainbow
scenes.task: Dorothy sings about a place far away. Listen for three things she hopes to find there.

scenes.title: The Munchkins
scenes.task: Look at the Munchkins and their clothes. What has changed about the film since the farm in Kansas?

scenes.title: Three friends on the road
scenes.task: The Scarecrow, the Tin Man and the Lion each want something. Write the three things.

scenes.title: Behind the curtain
scenes.task: Toto pulls the curtain open. Predict: who is the Wizard really, and what will Dorothy do?

words.def: a very strong wind that spins
words.ex: A tornado carries Dorothy's house away.

words.def: a woman with magic powers
words.ex: The Wicked Witch wants the ruby slippers.

words.def: the part of you that thinks
words.ex: The Scarecrow wants a brain.

words.def: being brave when you are afraid
words.ex: The Lion wants courage.

words.def: soft shoes for inside the house
words.ex: Dorothy wears red ruby slippers.

words.def: the place where you live
words.ex: Dorothy only wants to go home.

questions: Dorothy sings about a place 'over the rainbow'. What is your 'over the rainbow'?
The Scarecrow wants a brain, the Tin Man a heart and the Lion courage. Which is the most important? Why?
Would you walk to the Emerald City with these three friends? What would you ask them first?
In your country, what do people say when they want to go home?
The Wizard is only a man behind a curtain. Why does that matter?
Which character is the bravest? Give one example from the film.
Is this film scary for small children? Which part?
What would you say to Dorothy before she clicks her heels?

gaps.line: I'll get you, my pretty, and your little ___ too!
Lions and tigers and ___, oh my!
Pay no attention to that man behind the ___!

quotes.note: Dorothy says it at the end, and it is the film's message.

quotes.quote: I'll get you, my pretty, and your little dog too!
options: The Wicked Witch of the West
quotes.note: The witch says it to Dorothy and Toto.

quotes.quote: Pay no attention to that man behind the curtain!
quotes.note: The Wizard shouts it when Toto opens the curtain.

quiz.q: Where does Dorothy live at the start?
quiz.why: She lives on a farm in Kansas with Aunt Em and Uncle Henry.

quiz.q: How does Dorothy get to Oz?
quiz.why: A tornado lifts the house with Dorothy and Toto inside.

quiz.q: What does the Scarecrow want?
quiz.why: He thinks he has no brain, but he is the cleverest of the three.

quiz.q: What must Dorothy bring back to the Wizard?
quiz.why: He says he will help her if she brings the Wicked Witch's broomstick.

quiz.q: How does Dorothy finally get home?
quiz.why: Glinda tells her that the slippers can take her home.

roleplay.title: The Wizard's throne room
roleplay.setting: The Emerald City, a huge green room. A giant face floats in smoke above the throne.

roles.brief: You want to go home. You are tired, you are a little angry, and you have come a very long way to ask for help.
You speak in a big, slow voice and you hide behind smoke. You ask the same question three times.
You want a brain. You ask for it politely, and you explain why you need it.

roleplay.challenge: Play it twice: once with the Wizard terrifying, once with him obviously pretending. Which one is funnier?

quest.title: Station 1 · The shoes
quest.task: What colour are Dorothy's shoes, and who puts them on her feet?

quest.title: Station 2 · Word hunt
quest.task: Find three words for: a woman with magic, the part of you that thinks, and being brave when you are afraid.

quest.title: Station 3 · A fourth friend
quest.task: Invent a fourth friend for Dorothy. What is it made of, and what does it want? Act out the moment it joins the road.
quest.answer: Any new character with a material and a wish

quest.title: Station 4 · The road
quest.task: Put these in order: the tornado, the Munchkins, the Emerald City, the witch's castle.
quest.answer: tornado, Munchkins, Emerald City, witch's castle

title: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial
logline: A boy finds a small alien in his garden shed and hides him in his bedroom, while the two of them try to find a way home.
why: The story is told through faces and hands, and the children speak in short, everyday sentences. The alien repeats the same few words, so a beginner hears the same language twice and understands a little more each time.
language: American English with fast family talk; the alien speaks in a slow, strange voice with very few words.
content: Government agents with cars and guns chase the children, E.T. becomes very ill and seems to die, and there is a sad goodbye. Frightening for small children, fine for teenagers.

scenes.title: Something in the shed
scenes.task: What does Elliott see in the shed, and what does he take out with him?

scenes.title: E.T. learns to speak
scenes.task: Write down the first three words E.T. says. Who teaches him?

scenes.title: Halloween night
scenes.task: Gertie is a cowgirl. What are the other children wearing, and who stays at home?

scenes.title: The bikes fly
scenes.task: The children are stopped by cars and men. Predict: how will they get past them?

words.def: a person or thing from space
words.ex: E.T. is a small alien.

words.def: a small building in a garden
words.ex: Elliott finds E.T. in the shed.

words.def: to call someone on a telephone
words.ex: E.T. wants to phone home.

words.def: not healthy or well
words.ex: E.T. gets very sick.

words.def: a thing you do not tell anyone
words.ex: The children keep E.T. a secret.

words.def: the place beyond the sky
words.ex: E.T. comes from space.

questions: Elliott finds an alien in the garden. What would you do first: tell your parents or hide him?
Why do the children keep E.T. a secret from their mother?
In your country, what do children do if they find a hurt animal?
Would you like a friend from space? What would you show them in your town?
Gertie is small, and she is not afraid of E.T. Why not?
E.T. wants to phone home. What does 'home' mean for you?
E.T. says very few words. How does he show his feelings without them?
What would you say to E.T. when he leaves?

gaps.line: Is he a boy or a ___?

quotes.note: His most famous line: he wants to call his people and go home.
His last words, with a finger on Elliott's head: he will stay in Elliott's memory.
Elliott says it the moment his brother sees the alien.

quiz.q: Where does Elliott find E.T.?
quiz.why: He follows a noise outside and finds the alien hiding in the tool shed.

quiz.q: What does E.T. want to do?
quiz.why: He builds a machine to call his people.

quiz.q: What does E.T. drink that makes him strange?
quiz.why: He finds a beer in the fridge, and Elliott feels the effect at school.

quiz.q: Why does Elliott get ill?
quiz.why: The two are connected, so when E.T. becomes ill, Elliott does too.

quiz.q: How do the children escape from the agents?
quiz.why: E.T. lifts the bicycles into the air and over the roadblock.

roleplay.title: The secret in the bedroom
roleplay.setting: Elliott's bedroom, after school. Gertie has just seen E.T., and Michael has just walked in.

roles.brief: You want to keep E.T. safe. You must make the others promise to say nothing, and you are not sure you can trust them.
You are small, curious and terrible at keeping secrets. You ask the questions that nobody wants to answer.
You are the big brother. You think this is dangerous, but you really want to see the alien.

roleplay.challenge: Play it twice: once as a family argument, once as a spy film. Which one is easier to keep secret in?

quest.title: Station 1 · The wish
quest.task: What does E.T. want more than anything? Write the three words he says.

quest.title: Station 2 · Word hunt
quest.task: Find three words for: a small building in a garden, a thing you do not tell, and a person from another planet.

quest.title: Station 3 · A message home
quest.task: Write a short message from E.T. to his family on the back of a school book. Five words or fewer.
quest.answer: Any short message with a clear meaning

quest.title: Station 4 · The order
quest.task: Put these in order: the shed, the Halloween costumes, the flying bikes, the goodbye.

title: Despicable Me
logline: A supervillain who wants to steal the moon adopts three little girls to help him, and finds that being a dad is harder than being bad.
why: The plot is simple and visual: one plan, three girls, one big rocket. The minions speak almost no real language, so the story has to be understood through action, which is exactly what an A2 listener needs.
language: American English with quick comic voices; Gru has a heavy accent, the girls speak very clearly, and the minions speak a made-up language.
content: Cartoon violence: explosions, a shrink ray, and a girl in mild danger near the end. An orphanage, a bad neighbour and a lot of shouting are all played for laughs.

scenes.title: The plan
scenes.task: Listen to Gru explain his plan to the minions. What does he want to steal, and why?

scenes.title: Three girls
scenes.task: Watch the girls at the orphanage. What does each one want, and who is the bravest?

scenes.title: The shrink ray
scenes.task: Vector has the shrink ray. Predict: how will Gru get it back?

scenes.title: The recital
scenes.task: Gru is late for the girls' show. What does he do when he arrives, and how do the girls react?

words.def: a bad person in a story
words.ex: Gru is a villain with a big plan.

words.def: to take a child into your family
words.ex: Gru adopts three girls.

words.def: to make something smaller
words.ex: The ray can shrink a building.

words.def: the big light in the night sky
words.ex: Gru wants to steal the moon.

words.def: feeling good about what you did
words.ex: Gru is proud of the girls.

words.def: a list of things you will do
words.ex: Gru's plan has many steps.

questions: Gru wants to steal the moon. Is he a bad man, or a man who needs a family?
Which girl is most like you: Margo, Edith or Agnes? Why?
Would you like to live in Gru's house? What would you change about it?
In your country, what do people say about a man who lives alone?
The minions love Gru and never leave. Why do they stay?
Agnes wants a unicorn. What did you want most when you were small?
Which is funnier: the minions or Vector? Show one moment to the class.
What would you say to Gru the first time the girls call him 'Dad'?

gaps.line: Three little kittens, they lost their ___.
When the world needed a hero, they got a ___.
gaps.hint: a bad person in a story

quotes.note: Agnes says it about her toy unicorn, and it becomes the film's best-loved line.
The minions shout it whenever they are happy.

quotes.quote: I commit crimes with both direction and magnitude.
quotes.note: Vector introduces himself this way, and usually adds 'Oh, yeah!'

quiz.q: What does Gru want to steal?
quiz.why: He wants to shrink the moon and take it.

quiz.q: Why does Gru adopt the girls?
quiz.why: The girls sell cookies, and that gets him to Vector's door.

quiz.q: Who takes the shrink ray first?
quiz.why: Vector steals it from Gru at the start of the film.

quiz.q: What do the minions love?
quiz.why: They shout 'Banana!' and sing about them.

quiz.q: What does Gru do at the end?
options: He saves the girls and becomes their father
He flies away with the moon
He goes back to being a villain
quiz.why: He chooses the girls, and the moon goes back into the sky.

roleplay.title: The bedtime story
roleplay.setting: The girls' bedroom, night. Gru is reading 'Three Little Kittens' for the third time.

roles.brief: You are a villain, and you do not know how to read to children. You do all the animal voices badly and you want to leave.
You want one more story, and you know exactly how to get it. You are small, sweet and very difficult to refuse.
You are not sleepy. You ask difficult questions about the kittens and about Gru's job.

roleplay.challenge: Play it twice: once with Gru very scary, once with Gru very soft. Which one makes the girls sleep?

quest.title: Station 1 · The three girls
quest.task: Write the names of the three girls, from oldest to youngest.

quest.title: Station 2 · Word hunt
quest.task: Find three words for: a bad person in a story, to take a child into your family, and to make something smaller.

quest.title: Station 3 · A new minion
quest.task: Invent a minion. Give it a name, a favourite food and one job in Gru's laboratory.
quest.answer: Any named minion with a food and a job

quest.title: Station 4 · The plan
quest.task: Put these in order: the shrink ray is stolen, Gru adopts the girls, the girls' show, the moon comes back.
quest.answer: ray stolen, adoption, show, moon returns

title: Frozen
logline: Two sisters grow up apart because one of them has a secret power over ice, and on coronation day the secret gets out.
why: The songs repeat the key words again and again, and the story turns on three simple ideas: two sisters, fear, and a closed door. The dialogue is short and modern, and the pictures carry each new place.
language: American English, clear and quick; the songs are slower and repeat a lot, which makes them useful for listening practice.
content: The sisters' parents die at sea, a snow monster chases the heroes, and one character slowly freezes. Sad and a little frightening, but there is no blood.

scenes.title: Two sisters, one door
scenes.task: Watch the girls at the bedroom door. Why does Elsa close it, and what does Anna do?

scenes.title: The coronation
scenes.task: Listen to Anna and Hans. How many questions does Anna ask him in one minute?

scenes.title: Hans shows his plan
scenes.task: Hans stops being nice. What does he really want, and how does Anna react?

scenes.title: An act of true love
scenes.task: Pause before Anna runs to Elsa. Predict: who will save Anna, and how?

words.def: hard water that is very cold
words.ex: Elsa can turn water into ice.

words.def: a person made of snow
words.ex: Olaf is a friendly snowman.

words.def: a thing you do not tell anyone
words.ex: Elsa keeps her power a secret.

words.def: the feeling when you are afraid
words.ex: Elsa's fear makes her powers stronger.

words.def: to hold someone with your arms
words.ex: Anna wants to hug her sister.

words.def: the girl in your family
words.ex: Anna and Elsa are sisters.

questions: Elsa has a secret. Why is it so hard to tell Anna the truth?
Would you like to build a snowman with Olaf? What would you ask him?
In your country, do families talk about their feelings, or keep them inside?
Anna follows her sister alone. Is that brave or silly?
Which song stays in your head: 'Let It Go' or another one? Sing one line.
Hans says 'I love you', but he does not. How can you see that he is lying?
Which character changes the most: Elsa, Anna or Kristoff?
What would you say to Elsa at the coronation, if you were Anna?

gaps.line: Do you want to build a ___?

gaps.hint: you open it to go in

quotes.note: Elsa sings it when she stops hiding her power.

quotes.quote: Some people are worth melting for.
quotes.note: Olaf says it while he melts next to the fire.

quotes.quote: Do you want to build a snowman?
quotes.note: Anna sings it at Elsa's door, year after year.

quiz.q: What is Elsa's power?
quiz.why: She can make ice and snow with her hands.

quiz.q: Why does Elsa run away after the coronation?
quiz.why: Her magic turns the water to ice in front of everyone, and she runs away in fear.

quiz.q: Who is Kristoff's best friend?
quiz.why: Sven goes everywhere with him.

quiz.q: Who is really the villain?
quiz.why: Hans only wants the throne, and he says so to Anna when she is weak.

quiz.q: What saves Anna at the end?
options: An act of true love: she saves Elsa
quiz.why: Anna steps between Hans and Elsa, and that act of love saves her.

roleplay.title: Behind the door
roleplay.setting: Outside Elsa's bedroom door in the castle. Anna is eight, Elsa is twelve, and their parents have just left.

roles.brief: You want to play. You do not understand why the door is closed, and you ask the same question again and again.
You are afraid of your own hands. You must not open the door, and you cannot explain why.
You are the mother. You love both girls, you are scared, and you choose the easiest answer instead of the true one.

roleplay.challenge: Play it twice: once with Elsa silent, once with Elsa trying to explain. Which one is sadder?

quest.title: Station 1 · The kingdom
quest.task: What is the name of the kingdom, and what is the name of the snowman?

quest.title: Station 2 · Word hunt
quest.task: Find three words for: hard cold water, a thing you do not tell, and the feeling when you are afraid.

quest.title: Station 3 · A new verse
quest.task: Write one new verse for 'Do You Want to Build a Snowman?'. Three lines, from Anna's side of the door.
quest.answer: Any three lines about waiting at the door

quest.title: Station 4 · The order
quest.task: Put these in order: the coronation, 'Let It Go', Olaf's song, Hans's betrayal.
quest.answer: coronation, Let It Go, Olaf's song, Hans's betrayal
